video_caption: The video opens with a black screen featuring the white text "A Touch of Venus" in a decorative font at the center, accompanied by a small logo in the top right corner. The logo shows a white outline of a person embracing a globe filled with stars, with the text "A Touch of the Universe" (A Touch of the Universe) written below it. As the video progresses, the scene transitions to a screenshot of a website with a black background. A navigation bar appears at the top with options like "Home", "Project", "Team", "Downloads", "Tutorials", "Gallery", "Contact", and "Español Italiano" (Spanish Italian). The main title "A Touch of the Universe" is displayed on the left, followed by a paragraph of text explaining the project: "A Touch of The Universe" is a non-profit project for a tactile astronomy kit addressed to children with vision impairments. The first 30 kits were sent to educators and teachers in underdeveloped countries in Americas, Asia and Africa. We are currently working on an extension of the project, "A Touch of Venus" that includes a 3D tactile Venus globe along with an activity book and video tutorials." A larger version of the "A Touch of the Universe" logo is prominently featured on the right side of the screen. Finally, a white URL, "https://astrokit.uv.es", appears at the bottom center of the screen.

The video opens with the "International Astronomical Union | Office of Astronomy for Development" (IAU OAD) logo, featuring the letters "OAD" at the center of three broken, colored, concentric orbits with small blue, yellow, and green dots at their ends, set against a black background. The logo fades to reveal a light-colored wooden table laden with items. On the left side of the table sits a spherical, yellowish-orange, textured object resembling a planet (a Venus tactile globe) on a blue base. Next to it are two white, spiral-bound books, and a dark blue tote bag with a white illustration. A white sheet of paper is visible on the far left. The background consists of a light grey wall with a black vertical strip. The camera then zooms in on the white paper, displaying "INTRODUCTION TO THE KIT CONTENTS" and listing the project collaborators and details about the "A Touch of Venus" educational kit for both sighted and visually impaired individuals. Following this, a close-up shot of the tactile Venus globe highlights its textured surface and a prominent groove. The camera then focuses on one of the spiral-bound books titled ""A TOUCH OF VENUS" ACTIVITY BOOK," crediting authors, displaying an image of a textured white sphere, and showing logos for IAU OAD, Observatori Astronòmic, and VNIVERSITAT DE VALÈNCIA, along with licensing information. Finally, the camera moves to another white sheet of paper, titled "VENUS MODEL WITH FEATURE NAMES," which shows a diagram of a textured white sphere with various features labeled, accompanied by the same logos and licensing details, with the partially visible dark blue tote bag to its right.

The video begins with a close-up shot of a light brown wooden table. On the left side, there's a stack of white papers, with the top sheet displaying text that reads: "Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)". To the right, another white sheet of paper is visible, with partially legible text including "A Touch of Venus" and "This activity is funded by the IAU Office of Astronomy for Development (OAD). All materials have been produced under a Creative Commons Attribu- NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (CC BY-NC-SA". Stretched across the center of the table is a white ribbon decorated with small red, star-like motifs, appearing to be folded or knotted at regular intervals, creating segments. As the video progresses, a dark blue fabric tote bag is placed onto the table, covering part of the right-hand paper and the ribbon. The tote bag is adorned with white illustrations: a stylized celestial body, possibly a planet, surrounded by stars and an orbital path, with a small figure nearby. Above this imagery, the text "A Touch of the Universe" is written. Below the main design, three distinct logos are visible: a circular logo for "IAU OAD International Astronomical Union Office of Astronomy for Development", a logo featuring a ringed planet and the text "Observatori Astronòmic UNIVERSITAT D VALÈNCIA" (Astronomical Observatory, University of Valencia), and a crest-like emblem with "UNIVERSITAT D VALÈNCIA" (University of Valencia).

The video opens with a static shot of a light wooden table against a plain light gray wall. On the table, from left to right, there's a white document with text, followed by a yellow and orange textured spherical model, possibly a planet, resting on a small blue stand. Next are two open white booklets displaying images of a spherical object, and a white and red patterned ribbon or tape lying flat. To the far right, a dark blue canvas tote bag is visible, featuring a white graphic of a circular constellation and the English text "A Touch of the Universe," along with some logos. At 0:03, the URL "https://astrokit.uv.es" appears as a white text overlay at the bottom center of the screen. The camera then slowly zooms in on the spherical model, revealing a distinct split or opening on its surface.

The video opens with a close-up shot of a textured, yellow spherical object, resembling a planetary model, resting on a small blue base on a light wooden table. The sphere has a prominent, smooth circular area at what appears to be its North Pole and another similar, though less visible, area at its South Pole. A thin, raised line, representing a meridian, connects these two polar areas. The background consists of a plain light gray wall with a dark vertical strip. At the 0:33 mark, the sphere transitions into an open, spiral-bound notebook placed on the same wooden table. The left page of the notebook is visible and contains printed text, while the right page is blank. The text on the left page reads: "1. EXPLORING THE TACTILE VENUS MODEL. Objective: Participants will become familiar with the Venus tactile model by exploring it and learning how to use it. Age: Any. Duration: 15 minutes. Materials: Tactile Venus, measuring lace with knots. Activity Description: a. Procedure: Step 1: Present the tactile Venus to the participants and let them feel it to grasp a general idea. Step 2: Demonstrate how to identify the North Pole by locating the smooth shape of one of the polar caps."

The video opens with a static shot of an open, spiral-bound notebook lying on a light wooden table. The left page of the notebook is blank, while the right page is filled with printed text. The main heading on the right page reads "1. EXPLORING THE TACTILE VENUS MODEL." Below the heading, the text details the "Objective: Participants will become familiar with the Venus tactile model by exploring it and learning how to use it," followed by "Age: Any," "Duration: 15 minutes," and "Materials: Tactile Venus, measuring lace with knots." The section "Activity Description:" then introduces "a. Procedure:" which includes "Step 1: Present the tactile Venus to the participants and let them feel it to grasp a general idea" and "Step 2: Demonstrate how to identify the North Pole by locating the smooth shape of one of the polar caps." The camera holds this view for the entire duration of the segment.

The video features a spherical, textured model of Venus, predominantly yellow and orange with darker brown accents and a prominent circular patch on its top, resting on a light wooden table. Beside it lies an open, spiral-bound notebook detailing educational activities. The initial view shows the page titled "2. VENUS - Rotation," describing an activity for participants aged 10+ to explore the tactile Venus model and learn about its retrograde rotation movement, emphasizing identification of poles and surface features. As the narrative progresses, a dark blue fabric begins to cover the Venus model, and the notebook page changes to "3. VENUS - Global Warming," outlining an activity to simulate Venus's thick, cloud-covered atmosphere by completely concealing the model with the fabric, thus making its surface "invisible." The scene further transitions to show the blue fabric draped over roughly half of the Venus model, corresponding to the "4. VENUS - Phases" activity described in the notebook, which teaches about Venus's phases by covering half of the model to illustrate that only a portion can be felt or seen. The video concludes with a close-up shot of the yellow and orange Venus model, clearly showing a horizontal seam that divides it into two distinct halves, one slightly offset, and emphasizing the intricate, rough texture of its surface.

The video opens with a close-up of a yellowish-orange, textured spherical model, representing the planet Venus, with a smooth yellow band diagonally stretched across its surface. A person's hands then appear, holding the model and carefully wrapping a white ribbon adorned with small red stars and white flowers around its circumference, initially aligning it with the yellow band, while a white, spiral-bound notebook with printed text is visible in the blurred background. One hand points along the yellow band to various bumpy features on the sphere, identifying them as mountain ranges or volcanoes like Maxwell Montes, Rhea Mons, and Theia Mons. The hands then adjust the starred ribbon, demonstrating how to measure or locate specific points on the model by moving it along the "meridian" and then to a particular position to identify two distinct bumps. The scene widens to show the entire activity setup on a light wooden table: the textured Venus model resting on a blue stand, the open spiral-bound notebook, and two sheets of paper featuring four grey-scale images of spherical models. The notebook's visible text details "6. VENUS - modeling Volcanoes," stating the objective to demonstrate types of volcanoes on Venus, suitable for ages 6+, with a duration of 30 minutes, and materials including the "Tactile Venus Model," modeling materials (play dough, modeling clay, plasticine), and an "annotated map." The procedure outlines steps for creating and locating shield volcanoes on the model.

The video segment features a close-up view of a person's light-skinned hands interacting with a tactile, spherical model of Venus, which is textured and predominantly yellow/orange with some darker brown areas, sitting on a small blue circular base. An open, spiral-bound white notebook lies on a light-colored wooden table to the right, displaying text. The text on the page reads: "7. VENUS - surface, plans and highlands. Objective: This activity shows Venus geography and its main characteristics. The participants will explore the tactile Venus model and learn how to recognize plans and highlands by touching. Age: 6+ Duration: 30 min Materials: tactile Venus Model, measuring lace, annotated map. Activity Description: a. Procedure: Step 1: Present the tactile Venus to participants and ask them to turn them, North Pole Meridian towards them. Demonstrate how to find Lakshmi Planum, Sedna Planitia." (0:00-0:25) The hands are carefully positioning a white measuring tape, adorned with red asterisks and white stars, vertically along the model, from what appears to be its north pole downwards. (0:25-0:33) The hands then adjust the measuring tape horizontally around the model's "equator." (0:33-0:39) The measuring tape is removed, and the left hand gently feels a raised, textured region on the model. (0:39-0:54) The right hand's index finger points to a prominent, smoother, elongated raised feature that runs from the top of the model downwards, indicating a specific geographical characteristic. Throughout the segment, the person's hands are focused on demonstrating interaction with the model according to the instructions laid out in the notebook.

In a well-lit room, a person's hands are shown interacting with a textured, spherical yellow model, which resembles a planet. Initially, one hand points to various raised and depressed features on the model. The model sits on a blue stand next to an open, spiral-bound "A TOUCH OF VENUS" ACTIVITY BOOK. The book's visible page lists objectives, age range (8+), duration (1 hour), materials (Tactile Venus Model, lace with knots, annotated map), and an "Activity Description." Detailed bullet points explain geological terms like "terra" (highlands), "patera" (irregular crater), and "craters," along with examples of female figures after whom features on Venus are named, including Aphrodite, Ishtar, Lada, Guinevere, Sedna, Tinatin, and Atalanta. A subsequent close-up of the book (0:25-0:31) further details historical female figures: Cleopatra (Egyptian queen), Irène Joliot-Curie (French physicist, Nobel laureate), Maria Yermolova (Russian actress), Valentina Aleksandrovna Fedorets (Soviet astronomer), and Rosa Bonheur (French painter). The scene then returns to the hands as they use a white ribbon with small red flower patterns, representing a meridian, to measure distances and locate features on the spherical model. The ribbon is first aligned vertically and then horizontally across the model. The final shot reveals the complete setup: the yellow planet model with the ribbon around it, the activity book, a separate sheet of paper, and a blue fabric bag with a similar planet image and text, all resting on a light wooden table. The text on the book's cover reads: "A TOUCH OF VENUS" ACTIVITY BOOK by Amelia Ortiz-Gil, Lluisa Casas, Maria Jesus Moya, Alberto Fernandez-Soto, John Rorke & Andres Galvez, followed by logos and a Creative Commons license notice. A URL "https://astrokit.uv.es" is displayed at the bottom of the screen.

The video opens in an indoor setting, likely an office or classroom, with light grey walls and a dark vertical partition. On a light-colored wooden table, various items are displayed: a yellow-orange, mottled spherical model of a planet (presumably Venus) resting on a small blue stand, a white sheet of paper with printed text, two open spiral-bound booklets (also featuring images of a planet and text), a thin, striped white and reddish-brown object (possibly a ribbon), and a dark blue tote bag with a white graphic of a person looking at stars, along with the text "A Touch of the Universe" and other logos. At the bottom of the screen, the text "https://astrokit.uv.es" (This is a website address for an astrokit project from the University of Valencia) is visible from 0:02 to 0:07. A female voice is heard speaking. At 0:07, the scene transitions to a black screen. In the top right corner, a white logo of a stylized person looking at stars inside a circle appears, accompanied by the text "A Touch of the Universe". In the center of the screen, the title "A Touch of Venus" is displayed in white text. The female voice stops, and at 0:13, the screen transitions again to display white credits against the black background, listing "Script & Photography: Amelia Ortiz-Gil", "Music: Inspiring innovation by Adi Goldstein", "Voice over: Amelia Ortiz-Gil", "Editing: Fernando J. Ballesteros", "Recording: Xusa Moya", and "Technical support: Mónica Pallardó & Alberto Fernández-Soto". Below these credits, four white logos are displayed: "IAU" (International Astronomical Union), "OAD OFFICE OF ASTRONOMY FOR DEVELOPMENT", "Observatori Astronòmic UNIVERSITAT DE VALÈNCIA", and another logo (likely an abbreviation for Universitat de València). Soft instrumental music begins to play during this credit sequence.
